title: Lettre Tate (mai 66) (Cristaux) : lettre (1966), tapuscrit (s.d.), notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
The page is a very faint first draft, nearly illegible. The next page (p.64) is a clean rewrite of the same text, and the reconstruction relies on it.

Setting: S is a scheme of characteristic p.
- C is the category of finite étale group schemes E over S killed by p. Equivalently, these are locally constant sheaves of F_p-vector spaces of finite type, i.e. étale F_p-local systems.
- C' is the category of locally free O_S-modules M equipped with a Frobenius-linear isomorphism F_M : M^(p) = F_S^* M -> M. These are unit-root F-modules (F-crystals mod p with bijective Frobenius).
- The functor φ : C -> C' sends E to (E ⊗_{F_p} O_S, F_E ⊗ O_S). Here (E⊗O_S)^(p) ≅ E^(p)⊗O_S, and E^(p) is identified with E via the relative Frobenius F_{E/S}, an isomorphism because E is étale.

Proposition: φ is an equivalence of categories.

(a) Full faithfulness. Passing to internal Hom, it suffices to show that Γ(S,E) ≅ {x ∈ Γ(S, E⊗O_S) : F(x^(p)) = x}. By étale descent one reduces to E constant, then to E = F_p. This is exactness of the Artin–Schreier sequence 0 -> Z/p -> G_a -> G_a, with the last map x ↦ x^p − x.

(b) Essential surjectivity. Given (M,F), consider the map ℘(x) = F_M(x^(p)) − x on the vector group V(M).
- ℘ is an étale (smooth) epimorphism of group schemes: the term F_M(x^(p)) has zero differential, so d℘ = −1.
- Hence the kernel E is an étale group scheme killed by p.
- Finiteness reduces to showing its F_p-rank is locally constant, equal to rk M.
- That E⊗O_S -> M is an isomorphism can be checked fibrewise.
- This reduces to S = Spec k, k algebraically closed, which is Lang's theorem / the Artin–Schreier–Lang computation.

Purpose: this is the 'étale' part of a classification of p-torsion Barsotti–Tate-type groups by F-V-crystals mod p. It is used in the preceding pages on homomorphisms between étale and multiplicative-type p-groups and the duality triangle.
errors: No mathematical error is visible; the argument coincides with the corrected next page.
The notation 'F_S^* M^(p)' on this page is redundant, since M^(p) already denotes F_S^* M.

The finiteness of the kernel is only sketched: rank locally constant equal to rk M, then a fibrewise check. Locally it follows from the system A·x^(p) = x with A invertible, which defines a finite étale scheme of degree p^r.

ideas.what: Equivalence between étale F_p-local systems (finite étale p-torsion group schemes) and locally free O_S-modules with Frobenius isomorphism (unit-root F-modules), via E ↦ E⊗O_S and M ↦ ker(F−1)
ideas.modern_name: Katz's equivalence (mod p Riemann–Hilbert for unit-root F-crystals; Lang torsor)
ideas.usually_credited_to: N. Katz, 'p-adic properties of modular schemes and modular forms' (1973), Prop. 4.1.1, and SGA 7 Exp. XXII; rooted in Lang (1956) and Artin–Schreier
ideas.where_published: Not known in Grothendieck's own texts; the closest are SGA 7 (Katz's exposé) and the 1966 Tate letter context

ideas.what: Reduction of full faithfulness to exactness of the Artin–Schreier sequence via descent to constant E

deep.surprise_reason: This is a faint draft of the next page, giving the standard proof of the étale-F_p-sheaves versus unit-root F-modules equivalence. The result is well known and credited to Katz/Lang. At most there is mild historical interest in Grothendieck writing it out, possibly before Katz's 1973 publication, but the date is uncertain (s.d., possibly after 1970).
